validated_results.title: Vitamin C intake and risk of renal cell carcinoma: a meta-analysis.
validated_results.reason: This is a meta-analysis pooling published cohort and case-control studies rather than an original primary study.

validated_results.title: Phase II Drug-Metabolizing Polymorphisms and Smoking Predict Recurrence of Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Gene-Smoking Interaction.
validated_results.reason: The report centers on a genotype-stratified or gene-exposure interaction, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: [The biochemical carcinogenesis of selected heavy metals in bladder cancer].
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of biochemical mechanisms of heavy-metal carcinogenesis without original comparative data.

validated_results.title: Selenium Exposure and Cancer Risk: an Updated Meta-analysis and Meta-regression.
validated_results.reason: This is an updated meta-analysis and meta-regression of 69 published studies rather than a primary study.

validated_results.title: Comparative efficacy of vitamin D status in reducing the risk of bladder cancer: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
validated_results.reason: This is a systematic review with pairwise and network meta-analysis of previously published studies.

validated_results.title: STAT3 polymorphism rs4796793 may be a predictive factor of tumor response to multiple tyrosine kinase inhibitors in metastatic renal cell carcinoma in Japanese population.
validated_results.reason: The exposure is treatment with tyrosine kinase inhibitors and STAT3 genotype, not nutritional L-tyrosine, and the outcome is tumor response in existing metastatic disease.

validated_results.title: A decade of pharmacogenomics research on tyrosine kinase inhibitors in metastatic renal cell cancer: a systematic review.
validated_results.reason: This is a systematic review of pharmacogenomics of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy, not a primary nutritional exposure study.

validated_results.title: Bladder Cancer is Associated with Low Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D Concentrations in Tunisian Population.
validated_results.reason: Primary case-control study reporting adjusted odds of urothelial bladder cancer according to plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D status.

extraction.comparison_type: Vitamin D deficiency (25-OHD <30 nmol/L) versus sufficient concentrations
extraction.population: Tunisian patients with urothelial bladder cancer and healthy controls
extraction.smoking_status: Mixed (adjusted for smoking status and duration of smoking)

sample_size.excerpt: A case-control study included 250 patients with UBC and 250 healthy controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 250 + 250 = 500

cases.excerpt: A case-control study included 250 patients with UBC and 250 healthy controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Multivariate analysis showed that UBC is associated with vitamin D deficiency [odd-ratio (95% confidence interval), 3.71 (1.76-7.80); P = 0.001] and vitamin D insufficiency [2.65 (1.40-5.01); P = 0.003].

confidence_interval.excerpt: Multivariate analysis showed that UBC is associated with vitamin D deficiency [odd-ratio (95% confidence interval), 3.71 (1.76-7.80); P = 0.001] and vitamin D insufficiency [2.65 (1.40-5.01); P = 0.003].

comparison.excerpt: Vitamin D deficiency and insufficiency were defined as 25-OHD <30 nmol/L and 30 to 49.99 nmol/L, respectively.
